requirements.name: backend-driven collaboration mode preset discovery
key UX: The backend asks Codex for `collaborationMode/list` during startup and exposes the returned presets through runtime options.
Each preset carries a stable mode kind plus a user-facing label, with optional model and reasoning effort overrides when Codex provides them.
If Codex omits a display name, the product still shows a readable label generated from the mode key instead of hiding the preset.

requirements.name: mode selection in runtime settings
key UX: The runtime settings drawer includes a dedicated `Mode` selector alongside model, approval, sandbox, and reasoning settings.
The selected collaboration mode is stored in viewer-scoped runtime preferences so the user does not need to reselect it on every visit.
If a previously saved mode is no longer returned by the backend, the UI keeps it visible as `Unavailable: <mode>` instead of silently resetting the selection.

requirements.name: bootstrap and restore rules for collaboration mode
key UX: Stored collaboration mode preferences merge with backend runtime defaults rather than being discarded during bootstrap.
When a thread already exists, the restored session mode from the backend is treated as authoritative for that thread.
When bootstrapping without an existing thread, the product can fall back to the stored mode preference so the next send still uses the user's last choice.

requirements.name: per-turn collaboration mode submission
key UX: The next user message carries the currently selected collaboration mode through the chat send API instead of leaving mode as local-only UI state.
The backend splits collaboration mode from the rest of runtime settings and forwards it as a Codex `collaborationMode` payload on turn start.
If the current selection is cleared or unsupported, the send path can omit collaboration mode instead of forcing an invalid preset.

requirements.name: plan mode handoff to implementation mode
key UX: When the assistant finishes a plan turn and the thread is waiting for input, the latest plan item shows inline follow-up actions instead of forcing the user to type the next step manually.
Choosing `Implement plan` auto-submits `Implement the plan.` in `default` mode so execution continues outside of Plan mode.
Choosing `Stay in Plan mode` dismisses the shortcut without changing the current mode, and failed implementation auto-submits leave Plan mode selected so the user can retry.
